captions.hook_line: In 1919, a wave of molasses swept through Boston. It was deadly 🌊
captions.body: On January 15, 1919, a storage tank in Boston's North End burst and released about 2.3 million gallons of molasses. A wave estimated up to 25 feet high moved at about 35 mph, killing 21 people and injuring about 150. A court later found the company liable, and stricter building rules followed.

blocks.narration: Just after noon, its rivets popped like machine gun fire. Then a wave up to twenty-five feet tall tore loose.

blocks.narration: It rushed through the streets at about thirty-five miles an hour, bending the elevated railway and flattening whole buildings.
